newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF sees 1996 charge from restructuring.
newsitem.headline: BASF sees 1996 charge from restructuring.

text.p: German chemicals group BASF AG said on Wednesday restructuring costs would place a burden of around 600 million marks on its 1996 profits but this would be partially offset by favourable foreign exchange effects.
The company's chief financial officer, Max Dietrich Kley, told a news conference the restructuring charge had already been booked in the company's nine-month figures.
A positive contribution of around 300 million marks from exchange rate fluctuations could be set off against this, he added.
